children: Uplift Investors, a Darien, Connecticut-based private equity firm, said Thursday it has inked its sixth deal to invest in a law firm's back-office operations through a management services organization, this time with an Arkansas-based personal injury firm.
Uplift's Orion Legal MSO will provide back-office support such as administrative, finance, marketing and technology services to Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, which will still be owned by its attorneys.
Two of Rainwater's name partners — Mike Rainwater and Bob Sexton — will sit on Orion Legal's national advisory board.

"We believe Orion shares our values and understands what makes Rainwater special, and this partnership will allow us to build on what we’ve created while continuing to raise the bar for our clients and our team," Rainwater said in a statement released by Uplift.

Orion Legal, a portfolio company of Uplift that the small private equity firm launched in January, already provides back-office services to personal injury law firms operating in Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Rhode Island, Tennessee, and Texas.
Investors and other non-lawyers are broadly prohibited from ⁠owning direct stakes in US law firms or sharing in attorney fees.

The MSO model provides a vehicle for law firms to receive outside investments without breaching those professional rules — the firm spins off its non-legal, back-office operations into an MSO, which can be owned or partly owned by outside investors. The law firm pays the MSO from its revenues but does not share fees.
